advances: Small-radius regularity for strictly one-positive-vertex simplex caps, including moving physical vertices and cap parameters.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write the simplex $Q(W)=A_W K+t_W$ for an affine image of a fixed simplex, with $A_W$ invertible on a neighborhood of the reference matrix. A point of $Q(W)+\tau B_d$ has a unique nearest point in $Q(W)$. If that point lies in the relative interior of the face $F(W)$ of dimension $k$, its displacement $w$ lies in the normal cone of that face and has length at most $\tau$. The face and normal spaces are orthogonal, so each tube over a relative face interior uses the product of $k$-area and $(d-k)$-dimensional normal volume. These disjoint pieces, up to measure-null boundaries, exhaust the parallel body. The full-dimensional face contributes the original simplex volume or cap volume.

Let the positive vertex be $i$ and $h_j=u\cdot v_j(W)-b$. A face missing $i$ and its sufficiently thin tube are strictly outside the cap by the uniform negative margin. On a face containing $i$, translation by $w$ shifts all heights by $u\cdot w$, retaining their signs for uniformly small $\tau$. For $k\ge1$ the retained face piece is a simplex with $k$ edge scale factors, so its area is
$$
|F(W)|_k\,\frac{(h_i+u\cdot w)^k}{\prod_{j\in\operatorname{vert}F,\,j\ne i}u\cdot(v_i(W)-v_j(W))}.
$$
All denominators stay positive. For $k=0$ the selected vertex contributes its entire normal sector.

For $q=d-k>0$ use the fixed reference normal space $E_F$ and cone directions $\Theta_F=N_K(F)\cap S(E_F)$. The new cone is $A_W^{-T}N_K(F)$. With $L_W=A_W^{-T}|_{E_F}$ and its subspace Jacobian $J_W$, the parametrization
$$
w=\tau r L_W\theta/|L_W\theta|,\qquad
dw=J_W\tau^q|L_W\theta|^{-q}r^{q-1}\,dr\,d\sigma(\theta),
\qquad 0\le r\le1,\ \theta\in\Theta_F
$$
follows by linear change of variables and reference polar coordinates. Expand the retained numerator in powers of $\tau$ under this integral on a fixed domain. Powers range from $q$ to $q+k=d$. The coefficients are smooth in $W,u,b$ by differentiation under the integral, since the denominator bounds, invertibility and all the local parameter derivatives are uniform on smaller compact neighborhoods. For the total volume use the same argument with the full face area instead of the cap area. The full-dimensional face has the smooth unrounded contribution, and all other terms contain positive powers of $\tau$, giving the asserted $O(\tau)$ estimates. The same polynomial gives a joint smooth extension in $\tau$ for the implicit-function calculation, without needing a geometric negative-radius body.

In the plane, each adjacent edge strip contributes $\int_0^\tau L_{ij}(h_i+s\,u\cdot n_{ij})/D_{ij}\,ds$. The selected vertex adds $\theta_i\tau^2/2$, and the other vertex sectors contribute zero. This proves the explicit planar coefficients.
statement: Let $Q(W)$ be a labeled affine perturbation of a fixed $d$-simplex, with vertex matrix $W$ near the reference. Let a cap $H=\{x:u\cdot x\ge b\}$ have exactly one positive vertex, indexed by $i$, and all other vertices negative, with uniform strict margins on the parameter neighborhood. Then $|Q(W)+\tau B_d|$ and $|(Q(W)+\tau B_d)\cap H|$ are polynomials of degree at most $d$ in sufficiently small $\tau\ge0$, with smooth coefficients in $W,u,b$. Their parameter derivatives through order two converge uniformly to the unrounded ones with error $O(\tau)$ on smaller compact neighborhoods. In $d=2$, writing $h_i=u\cdot v_i-b$, $D_{ij}=u\cdot(v_i-v_j)$, and using adjacent edge lengths $L_{ij}$, outward unit normals $n_{ij}$ and exterior vertex angle $\theta_i$, the cap polynomial has linear coefficient $\sum_{j\ne i}L_{ij}h_i/D_{ij}$ and quadratic coefficient $[\theta_i+\sum_{j\ne i}L_{ij}(u\cdot n_{ij})/D_{ij}]/2$.
title: Smooth radius polynomials for rounded simplex corner caps
